svg.text: Civic HVAC node: ESP32 DevKitC + 12x AQY212 PhotoMOS dial emulator
2000 Honda Civic climate board, dials removed. Each dial pad set is COM + A/B/C/D. Every relay closes COM to one code pad.
Keep under ~1 m. Twist SDA with GND, SCL with GND.
Skip R13/R14 if the S3 bus already has pull-ups.
AQY212 (DIP-4): pin 1 = LED anode, pin 2 = LED cathode, pins 3 and 4 = switch output (either way round).
Each relay: ESP32 GPIO → 330 Ω → pin 1, pin 2 → ESP32 GND, pin 4 → that dial's COM pad, pin 3 → that dial's A/B/C/D pad.
All four pin-4 wires of one dial join at that dial's COM pad (shown as the FAN COM / MODE COM / TEMP COM labels).
Remove the original dials, or they will short the codes. Solder wires to the empty dial pads (COM, A, B, C, D are printed on the board).
The relay outputs are isolated: no wire from the ESP32 goes to the climate board except through the relays.
The climate board stays on its 3 factory plugs, powered by the car as before.
Ground symbols on the left side of each relay are ESP32 GND. LED current ≈ 6.5 mA per relay, 78 mA max total.
TVS diode D1: band (cathode) towards +12 V. The fuse protects the node wiring; use a fuse tap on an ignition-switched circuit.
